residual_risk: The heartbeat and branch-override lines are brief-level, not enforced code: a subagent that ignores them can still be reclaimed as stale or push to the wrong branch — same caveat as the existing verb-check known gap.

gc's PR-merged/closed check for agent-* worktrees depends on closedByPullRequestsReferences (caps.closedByPrs); on a GitHub schema without it, these worktrees fall back to accumulating until the task itself settles (sweepTask still cleans them then).

Item 5 from the issue (the daemon-leaked KB_TASK / attemptIdentity gap, #150) is documented as a known gap in tracks.md but not fixed in this PR — it needs its own attemptIdentity/subagentStopHook change, out of this task's file scope.

results.summary: Filled in the sentences the fan-out track brief was still missing (PR #194/#129 review): the per-node subagent brief now tells each child to heartbeat the root (not itself) every ~10 minutes, since the orchestrator's own turn ends the moment it spawns a wave and cannot wake itself; it overrides hkb context's current-branch line (the child's checkout is a throwaway agent-<id> one, not the node's kb/<n>); and the wave loop names the fallback when a spawn itself fails (work the node yourself sequentially, or hkb block --kind transient). gc gains agentWorktreeNode/sweepAgentWorktrees so an agent-<id> worktree a committed subagent left behind is swept once its kb/<n> branch's PR merges or closes, from both hkb gc and sweepTask. Softened the 'deleted when you finish' line in the brief and docs/harnesses.md to match reality. tracks.md gained two Known-gaps entries: the heartbeat-skip stale-reclaim risk, and the daemon-leaked KB_TASK (#150) that can suppress the root's Stop.
